PA-2025-HB2887.title: An Act amending Title 53 (Municipalities Generally) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in employees, providing for emergency responder benefits for surviving family members.

actions.text: Referred to Veterans Affairs & Emergency Preparedness

PA-2025-HB2887.aiSummary: The bill would add rules in Pennsylvania law for emergency responder benefits for surviving family members. It would affect surviving family members of emergency responders.

PA-2025-SB509.title: An Act amending Title 75 (Vehicles) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in general provisions, further providing for definitions; in rules of the road in general, further providing for maximum speed limits, providing for maximum speed limits enforced by local law enforcement officers with RADAR and further providing for speed timing devices; and imposing penalties.

votes.motion: Committee vote (Transportation): Reported as Amended A04561

PA-2025-SB509.aiSummary: The bill would let local police use RADAR to check vehicle speeds on local roads, and on state roads if allowed by a state agency. It would set new speed rules, add fines for speeding, and require warning signs, training, and a marked police vehicle before RADAR use. It would also limit how much money towns can keep from these fines and require audits of that money.

PA-2025-HR672.title: A Resolution urging the Federal Government to condemn the rioting and civil unrest in France and across Europe, expressing solidarity with the people of France and of our European allies and reaffirming the principles of secure borders, the rule of law and the protection of God-given rights and property.
PA-2025-HR672.aiSummary: The resolution would ask the federal government to condemn rioting and civil unrest in France and other parts of Europe. It would also express support for the people of France and other European allies, and say Pennsylvania stands for secure borders, the rule of law, and protecting property and rights. Copies would be sent to U.S. and Pennsylvania officials, including the French ambassador to the United States.

PA-2025-HB2865.title: An Act amending Title 75 (Vehicles) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in liquid fuels and fuels tax, further providing for diesel fuel importers and transporters, prohibiting use of dyed diesel fuel on highways and violations and penalties.
PA-2025-HB2865.aiSummary: The bill would update rules for dyed diesel fuel in Pennsylvania. It would require notices on certain sales and pumps, and it would keep dyed diesel out of motor vehicles on public highways unless federal law or a presidential executive order allows it. It would also change penalties and take effect right away.

PA-2025-HB2593.title: An Act amending the act of April 9, 1929 (P.L.177, No.175), known as The Administrative Code of 1929, in general provisions relating to powers and duties of the Department of Health and its departmental administrative and advisory boards, providing for prostate health public education campaign; and establishing the Prostate Health Public Education Campaign Fund.

votes.motion: Committee vote (Appropriations): Re-report Bill As Committed
Committee vote (Health): Report Bill As Amended

PA-2025-HB2593.aiSummary: The bill would require the state Health Department to run a public education campaign on prostate health and prostate cancer screening. It would share plain-language information on risk factors, screening tests, signs, and early treatment, and it would reach people through public ads, community forums, health offices, providers, and other groups. The campaign would also have materials in English, Spanish, Vietnamese, Mandarin Chinese, and other languages the department chooses, and it would be funded by a new state fund for this purpose.

PA-2025-SR402.title: A Resolution recognizing and congratulating the Pennsylvania Chamber of Business and Industry on being named the 2026 State Chamber of the Year by the National Association of State Chambers.
PA-2025-SR402.aiSummary: A Senate resolution would recognize and congratulate the Pennsylvania Chamber of Business and Industry for being named the 2026 State Chamber of the Year by the National Association of State Chambers. It also would commend the group for its work on issues like tax reform, permitting, workforce development, energy, and infrastructure. The resolution affects the chamber and its work on behalf of Pennsylvania businesses.

PA-2025-HB1633.title: An Act amending Title 75 (Vehicles) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in general provisions, further providing for definitions; in licensing of drivers, further providing for examination of applicant for driver's license; in special vehicles and pedestrians, providing for electric scooters and for shared electric scooters; and imposing penalties.

votes.motion: Committee vote (Appropriations): Re-report Bill As Committed
MOTION TO APPEAL RULING OF THE CHAIR
Committee vote (Transportation): Report Bill As Amended

PA-2025-HB1633.aiSummary: The bill would let certain cities set up shared electric low-speed scooter programs with private scooter companies. It sets rules for where scooters can be used, how fast they can go, age limits, lights at night, insurance, reports, and fines for rule breaks. It also says these shared scooters would not need title or registration papers and would not count as motor vehicles.

PA-2025-SB806.aiSummary: This law updates Pennsylvania’s consumer protection rules by saying that people who make or share AI-generated content must clearly say it was made using artificial intelligence. The disclosure must be easy to notice and shown in the same form as the content, such as text, images, audio, or video. It also defines artificial intelligence and sets rules for what counts as a clear and visible disclosure. The law took effect 60 days after enactment.

PA-2025-SB1485.title: An Act amending Title 3 (Agriculture) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in race horse industry reform, further providing for additional powers of commission.

votes.motion: Committee vote (Appropriations): Re-report Bill As Committed

Committee vote (Agriculture & Rural Affairs): Reported as Committed

PA-2025-SB1485.aiSummary: The act changes the rules for racing licenses in Pennsylvania by expanding background checks for people applying to work in horse racing. It requires fingerprint-based criminal history checks for applicants in jobs tied to horse care, racing, wagering systems, security, and racing management, including many named roles like trainers, jockeys, stewards, and veterinarians. It became Act No. 116 of 2026 and took effect right away.

PA-2025-HB559.aiSummary: The bill would add a new term for a place that has never had certain liquor licenses, or has not been used for a non-license business for at least three years. It would change how the Liquor Control Board handles some new license applications and transfers to these places, including hearings and nearby resident testimony. It would also let distributor license holders sell malt or brewed beverages in any amount for off-site use, and allow refillable growlers.

PA-2025-HB2227.aiSummary: This act became law and names many bridges and highway sections across Pennsylvania for local people, veterans, firefighters, and other honorees. It also creates the Pennsylvania and National Medal of Honor Highway. The Department of Transportation must put up and keep signs showing the new names, and the law took effect 60 days after enactment.

PA-2025-HB1006.title: An Act amending the act of April 28, 1937 (P.L.417, No.105), known as the Milk Marketing Law, in weighing and testing, further providing for certified testers and for certified weighers and samplers.

votes.motion: Committee vote (Agriculture & Rural Affairs): Reported as Committed
Committee vote (Appropriations): Re-report Bill As Committed
Committee vote (Rules): Re-report Bill As Committed
Committee vote (Agriculture & Rural Affairs): Report Bill As Committed

PA-2025-HB1006.aiSummary: The law updates milk testing and sampling rules under Pennsylvania’s Milk Marketing Law. It lets certified testers and certified weighers and samplers hold their certificates for up to two years instead of one, and it changes some fee references to the Milk Marketing Fee Act. People who test, weigh, or sample milk for dealers would be affected, and the law takes effect 60 days after approval.
